note: Fuzzer creates a function-based buffer source wrapping the raw input bytes; this source is not layered (src->src == NULL) and has refcount 1.
The buffer source is passed to zip_open_from_source; the archive takes ownership of the source and stores it as za->src.
Opens the buffer source (open_count becomes 1) before parsing the central directory; the source is a function source so no recursion occurs here.
Calls zip_source_stat on the buffer source to obtain the archive size; since the source is not layered, it directly invokes the buffer read_data callback with ZIP_SOURCE_STAT.
Seeks the buffer source to the end minus CDBUFSIZE to locate the End of Central Directory record; the source is still open.
When the EOCD64 locator magic is found before the EOCD record, _zip_read_eocd64 is invoked to parse the ZIP64 end-of-central-directory record.
Reads the 56-byte EOCD64 record from the source; this calls _zip_read which calls zip_source_read on the buffer source.
The central directory entries are read into a buffer; each entry's compression method, sizes, and encryption method are parsed from the central directory.
The parsed central directory entries are stored in the zip_t structure; entry 0 has a non-STORE compression method (e.g., deflate) and a size smaller than the full file size.
The fuzzer opens entry i with flags=0; this calls zip_fopen_index_encrypted which invokes zip_source_zip_file_create to build a layered source chain for reading the entry data.
For a compressed entry with partial data, src is set to the archive's buffer source (za->src) which has refcount 1 from the archive.

A window source W1 is created wrapping the archive buffer source. _zip_source_window_new calls zip_source_layered_create (which no longer keeps the lower source) and then zip_source_keep(src), so the buffer source refcount becomes 2.

code: window_source = zip_source_layered_create(src, window_read, ctx, error); if (window_source != NULL) { zip_source_keep(src); }
note: The window source W1 is created with W1->src pointing to the buffer source. zip_source_keep increments the buffer source refcount to 2; the caller's reference to the buffer source is not freed in the new ownership model.
A decompress source D is created wrapping W1. zip_source_layered_create no longer calls zip_source_keep, so W1's refcount stays at 1; ownership of W1 is transferred to D.
A CRC source C is created wrapping D. zip_source_layered_create does not keep D, so D's refcount stays at 1; ownership of D is transferred to C.

Because partial_data is true and needs_decompress is true, a second window source W2 is created wrapping C. _zip_source_window_new calls zip_source_layered_create (no keep) then zip_source_keep(C), so C's refcount becomes 2.

The final source returned is W2. The caller's reference to C (refcount 2) is never freed because the zip_source_free(src) call was removed in regression commit 4a0b206b; C now has one leaked reference from the caller and one from W2.
zip_source_open is called on W2. Since W2 is layered, it recursively calls zip_source_open(W2->src) which is C, then D, then W1, then the buffer source. The recursion opens each layer in the chain.

The recursive zip_source_open calls dereference src->src for each layered source. If any lower source in the chain has been freed due to the refcount mismatch, this read of src->src triggers the heap-use-after-free.

The innermost zip_source_open reads src->src from a freed zip_source_t structure. ASAN reports a heap-use-after-free READ 1 at the address of the freed source's src field, matching the crash signature zip_source_open -> zip_source_open -> _zip_open.
